title: Anthropic transport with separated credentials and bounded retry

outcomes.statement: Anthropic requests use one endpoint-policy module and share bounded per-vendor-account rate and retry budgets, including non-replay of ambiguous invite creation.
outcomes.demo: Against deterministic transport fixtures with an injected clock, User Management and Analytics calls carry their declared headers, bursts respect 100/min and 60/min budgets, invite traffic respects 1200/hour, and bounded retries consume the same budget.

outcomes.statement: Invalid Admin or Analytics credential configurations fail closed before transport.
outcomes.demo: Missing, blank, duplicate, identical, unhealthy, and wrong-kind credential fixtures each return a deterministic rejection while the network-call counter remains zero.

uncertainties.statement: No live Anthropic credentials or invite-canary authorization are available.
uncertainties.resolution: This child uses deterministic transport fixtures. Real credential scope, organization binding, and provider behavior remain exclusively in US-054 and cannot be claimed here.

uncertainties.statement: Retries could amplify traffic or replay an invite whose provider outcome is ambiguous.
uncertainties.resolution: Initial attempts and retries consume one injected-clock limiter; only safe reads and idempotent deletes retry bounded 429/5xx classes, and ambiguous invite creation is never automatically replayed.

uncertainties.statement: The connector package has no runtime rate-limit dependency and its tests must remain deterministic.
uncertainties.resolution: Implement the limiter against an injected clock inside the provider transport boundary, preserving the dependency-free package and deterministic verification.

dependencies.reason: The connector-call journal is integrated with the transport attempt seam delivered here.
